t.6.17.1: Having heard those wholesome and courageous words spoken by Sāraṇa, King Rāvaṇa replied to Sāraṇa.
t.6.17.2: Even if the gods, Gandharvas and Dānavas were to attack me, I would never give up Sītā, not even out of fear of all the worlds.
t.6.17.3: But you, gentle one, badly frightened and utterly defeated by the monkeys, think it right to give Sītā back this very day. For what rival is there who could conquer me in battle?
t.6.17.4: Having spoken these harsh words, Rāvaṇa, the glorious lord of the rākṣasas, then climbed, out of a desire to see, a palace white as snow and as tall as many palm trees.
t.6.17.5: Rāvaṇa, accompanied by those two spies and overwhelmed with rage, gazing upon the ocean, the mountains and the forests, beheld the region of the earth completely filled with monkeys.
t.6.17.6: Beholding that great army of the monkeys, boundless and beyond counting, King Rāvaṇa questioned Sāraṇa.
t.6.17.7: Among these chiefs of the monkeys, who are the heroes, who are the mighty ones? Who are those of great zeal who advance in the forefront on every side?
t.6.17.9: Then Sāraṇa, who knew who the chief ones were, heeding the words of the lord of the Rākṣasas as he questioned him, pointed out to him those foremost forest-dwellers.
t.6.17.8: To whom does Sugrīva listen, and who are the leaders of the troop-leaders? Sāraṇa, tell me everything: who are the foremost among the monkeys?
t.6.17.10: This monkey who stands roaring, facing Laṅkā, is surrounded by a hundred thousand troop leaders.
t.6.17.11: By whose mighty roar all of Laṅkā trembles, together with its ramparts and gateways, its mountains, forests and groves.
t.6.17.12: This heroic troop-leader named Nīla stands at the front of the army of the great-souled Sugrīva, lord of all the monkeys.
t.6.17.13: The mighty one who, raising up his arms, strides over the earth on his feet, facing Laṅkā, and in his anger yawns again and again.
t.6.17.14: Like a mountain peak and with the hue of lotus filaments, he, enraged, lashes his tail again and again.
t.6.17.15: He by the sound of whose tail the ten directions seem to resound, this one, named Aṅgada, consecrated as heir apparent by Sugrīva, king of the monkeys, challenges you to battle.
t.6.17.16: But those bulls among monkeys who, stiffening their limbs, roar and bellow, and who, rising up, stretch themselves in wrath.
t.6.17.18: The heroes who follow him are dwellers of the sandalwood forests; this one hopes to crush Laṅkā with his own army.
t.6.17.17: These are hard to withstand, terrible and fierce, of fierce valor; they number eight hundred thousand and ten hundred crores.
t.6.17.20: Swiftly approaching Sugrīva, the monkey goes forth again, dividing the monkey army and gladdening its divisions.
t.6.17.19: Śveta, gleaming like silver, mighty and of fearsome prowess, is a wise and valiant monkey, renowned throughout the three worlds.
t.6.17.21: He who of old used to roam the delightful mountain on the bank of the Gomatī, the mountain called by name Saṃkocana, abounding in many kinds of trees.
t.6.17.22: There this troop-leader named Kumuda rules the kingdom, he who leads a thousand times a hundred thousand monkeys.
t.6.17.23: He of terrible deeds is the one whose hairs, many fathoms long, cling to his long tail and lie spread out, copper-red, yellow, pale and white.
t.6.17.24: Undaunted, wrathful and fierce, he longs for battle; this very one hopes to crush Laṅkā with his own army.
t.6.17.25: But this one, who resembles a lion, tawny and long-maned, gazes steadily at Laṅkā, as though wishing to burn it with his eye.
t.6.17.26: O king, this troop-leader named Rambha constantly dwells upon the Vindhya, Kṛṣṇagiri, Sahya, and the mountain Sudarśana.
t.6.17.27: A hundred and thirty hundred-thousands of monkey troop-leaders surround him and follow him, intent on crushing Laṅkā by their might.
t.6.17.28: But he who opens wide his ears and yawns again and again, who does not tremble before death and does not run away from the troop,
t.6.17.29: O King, the troop-leader named Śarabha, mighty and free from fear, constantly dwells on the delightful Śālveya mountain.
t.6.17.31: But he who stands there, mighty, covering the sky like a cloud, in the midst of the heroic monkeys, like Vāsava among the gods,
t.6.17.30: O king, the troop-leaders of this mighty one, all known as the Vihāras, likewise number forty hundred thousand.
t.6.17.33: This one, who dwells on Pāriyātra, the most excellent of mountains, is the troop-leader named Panasa, ever hard to withstand in battle.
t.6.17.32: He whose great and terrible din, like the booming of kettledrums, is heard here, the clamor of the lords of the monkeys eager for battle…
t.6.17.34: Fifty hundred-thousand troop leaders, each with his own troops arranged in separate divisions, wait upon this one, the foremost of troop leaders.
t.6.17.35: He who stands there adorning the fearsome, surging army that is stationed on the shore of the ocean, like a second sea.
t.6.17.36: This troop-leader named Vinata, who resembles Mount Dardara, roams about drinking from the Parṇāśā, the finest of rivers.
t.6.17.37: His army consists of six million monkeys; the troop-leader named Krathana challenges you to battle.
t.6.17.38: And that monkey who bears a body with the hue of red ochre is the mighty Gavaya, who in his wrath advances against you.
t.6.17.39: Seventy hundred-thousands attend upon him; he hopes to crush Laṅkā with his own army.
t.6.17.40: These are troop-leaders, the foremost among troop-leaders, hard to withstand, fearsome, mighty, and able to take any form at will; their number cannot be reckoned.
